contents.name: Equation (10.1): the nonlinear Tikhonov functional with alpha>0 and reference x0
Weakly closed graph and nonempty weakly closed-domain assumptions

Theorem 10.1: global Tikhonov minimizer existence by the direct method
Theorem 10.2: fixed-alpha weak-cluster stability for strongly convergent data
contents.reason: The source also proves strong convergence when the limiting minimizer is unique; the authored theorem keeps only the weak-cluster claim and does not assume uniqueness.

contents.name: Theorem 10.3: vanishing-noise convergence under alpha->0 and delta^2/alpha->0
contents.reason: The authored claim keeps the planned weak-cluster conclusion and the exact-solution/minimum-norm conditions; the source additionally proves strong subsequence convergence.

contents.name: Theorem 9.9: local minimum-norm uniqueness under a tangential cone condition
contents.reason: Its differentiability and local tangential-cone hypotheses are not premises of global nonlinear Tikhonov existence or stability.

contents.name: Theorem 10.3 strong-subsequence and full-sequence uniqueness conclusions
contents.reason: The authored vanishing-noise item retains the planned weak-cluster minimum-norm conclusion and makes no uniqueness or strong-convergence claim.

sources.title: Benedikt Wirth, Inverse Problems (complete University of Münster course notes)
sources.locator: Chapter 10, Definition 83 and Theorems 85-87, including their proof discussions (PDF pp. 18-20; 56-page notes).

contents.name: Definition 83: least-squares/minimum-norm solutions and nonlinear Tikhonov functional
contents.reason: The source uses the equivalent objective with both terms scaled by 2; its Hilbert-space and domain convention is compared in the notes.

contents.name: Theorem 85(a): direct-method existence under reflexivity, continuity, and weak sequential continuity of F
contents.reason: This is an independent treatment under stronger operator assumptions; the authored proof uses sequential weak-to-weak graph closedness.

contents.name: Theorem 85(b): exact solutions admit an x0-minimum-norm solution under the same stronger operator assumptions
contents.reason: The source gives a direct-method outline; the authored item verifies every direct-method hypothesis and proves the application.

contents.name: Theorem 86: weak-cluster stability for fixed alpha under the source's stronger continuity assumptions
Theorem 87: vanishing-noise x0-minimum-norm cluster points with delta/sqrt(alpha)->0
contents.reason: The parameter condition is algebraically equivalent to delta^2/alpha->0 for nonnegative delta and positive alpha; the source again assumes stronger operator regularity.

contents.name: Remark 84: nonlinear Tikhonov minimizers need not be unique, and local/global minima may differ
Corollary 89: strong stability/convergence in Hilbert spaces
contents.reason: The controlling design requests weak-cluster conclusions and warns that uniqueness is not general; this stronger source result is not imported.
